scope: forty-third batch: the first master-data slice — the buyer-to-client matching layers and the attribution decision ladder, with all data access injected so the core is fully offline-verifiable

live_source.start_capture_note: no separate start capture was taken this batch; the before-snapshot is the forty-second batch delivery, which proves the live source did not change between that delivery and this one, not the identity at the moment work started
live_source.delivery_compare_command: cowork-migration-baseline.py compare baseline-forty-second-delivery.json baseline-forty-third-delivery.json (before pinned at 7ea12219, after pinned at 2e21cbb0)
live_source.source_note: the ported core is pure; the pinned code is executed against a fake database in the differential

covers: candidate conflict: one candidate, duplicates, an abbreviation of the same name, two unrelated buyers, empty strings
tax normalisation removes dashes and spaces, and only thirteen digits are valid
each of the six matching layers, including the tax layer being skipped below ten digits and the exact layers returning before any approximation
a substring keeping its length ratio as confidence, the best approximation winning, and nothing similar returning nothing

all five decisions: nothing to do, conflicting candidates to review without creating, a tax hit assigned and learned, a memory hit assigned, a new valid tax created and learned, a failed creation going to review, a near name only suggested (never bound, never learned), no tax and no match to review
a short tax number not being valid so no client is created, an exactly matching short name staying in the suggestion band rather than the auto-assign band, and the learner being optional

checks.note: the pinned module talks to a database, so the database is the device replaced: a fake cursor answers exactly the three queries the pinned code issues (the learned memory row, the tax-id row, the active-client list) and the two write paths are recording stubs. Each batch compares the six decision fields, the learn calls (count and arguments) and the create-by-tax call arguments; the conflict rule is compared separately over 24 name pairs. Floors sit just under the measured coverage so a fixture that stops reaching a branch is caught.

checks.command: docker exec ... python -m unittest test_cowork_buyer_resolve test_cowork_document_tier test_cowork_reconciliation_bank_intake test_cowork_bank_sheets test_cowork_reconciliation_gl_sheets test_cowork_reconciliation_bank_model_path test_cowork_reconciliation_bank_reread
checks.note: the new module is independent of the OCR work, so the previous batches' suites are run to confirm nothing regressed

intentional_differences: the pinned functions open their own cursors; this side takes the scoped memory hit, the active client list, a create-by-tax-id callback and a learn callback, which is what makes the core verifiable offline
update_history_client_id is not ported: writing the client id back onto a recognition record belongs to the history domain, which already carries the attribution field
the table bootstrap and the client/store CRUD (list, get, create, update, delete) and the supplier-category memory are the next master-data batch

the tax comparison normalises both sides the same way (stripping surrounding spaces as well), which differs from the pinned client-side comparison only for a stored tax id with surrounding spaces; the differential fixture has none and the difference is recorded
comments and docstrings were rewritten; every threshold, every layer order, every returned string and every reason code is the deployed one
not_run: any storage layer (this batch is the pure decision core), the client roster RPCs, the import normalisation, the product and supplier master data, real invoice data, the frontend, deployment, external results and user acceptance
